name: The prince of Tyre
charge: Saying, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God
summary: Ezekiel's word to the ruler of the merchant city: because thine heart is lifted up, and thou hast said, I am a God, in the midst of the seas; yet thou art a man, and not God. Wiser than Daniel, richer by his traffick, and undone by both.
offense: Self-deification on the strength of trade. By the multitude of thy merchandise they have filled the midst of thee with violence, and thou hast sinned. Tyre had also rejoiced at Jerusalem's fall: aha, she is broken, I shall be replenished.
judgment: They shall bring thee down to the pit, and thou shalt die the deaths of them that are slain in the midst of the seas. Wilt thou yet say before him that slayeth thee, I am God? Nebuchadnezzar besieged the mainland city; Alexander finished the island.

entries.commentary: The Most High tells Ezekiel to say to the prince of Tyrus that because his heart is lifted up and he has said, I am a god, I sit in the seat of God in the midst of the seas, yet he is a man and not God. Though he set his heart as the heart of God and was wiser than Daniel, getting riches by his wisdom and traffic, the Most High will bring strangers upon him, the terrible of the nations, to bring him down to the pit and die the deaths of the uncircumcised by the hand of strangers.

Ezekiel takes up a lamentation upon the king of Tyrus, who was full of wisdom and perfect in beauty, in Eden the garden of God, covered with every precious stone, the anointed cherub upon the holy mountain of God, perfect in his ways until iniquity was found in him. By the multitude of his merchandise he was filled with violence and sinned, his heart lifted up because of his beauty; therefore the Most High casts him out as profane, brings forth a fire from the midst of him, and brings him to ashes in the sight of all who behold him.

The word comes against Zidon, that the Most High will be glorified in the midst of her, sending pestilence and blood into her streets and executing judgments, and they shall know that He is the Lord. There shall be no more a pricking briar nor grieving thorn to the house of Israel from those round about who despise them; when the Most High gathers Israel from the people and is sanctified in them, they shall dwell safely in the land given to His servant Jacob, build houses, and plant vineyards.

In the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, the word comes because Tyrus said against Jerusalem, Aha, she that was the gate of the peoples is broken and turned to me, so I shall be replenished now she is laid waste. Tyrus saw our loss of Jerusalem as their come-up and profit. Therefore the Most High is against Tyrus and will cause many nations to come up against her like the sea casting up its waves; they shall destroy her walls, break her towers, scrape her dust, and make her like the top of a rock, a place for spreading nets, and her daughters in the field shall be slain.

The Most High will bring Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, a king of kings from the north, with horses, chariots, and horsemen, to slay her daughters, build a fort, cast a mount, and set engines of war against her walls and towers. Babylon serves as His sword against the nations that thought our downfall was their gain. His horses shall cover her with dust and tread down her streets; he shall slay her people, spoil her riches, prey on her merchandise, break her walls, destroy her pleasant houses, and lay her stones, timber, and dust in the midst of the water. He will cause the noise of her songs to cease and make her like the top of a rock, a place to spread nets, built no more. -

At the sound of Tyrus's fall the isles shall shake and the wounded cry, and all the princes of the sea shall come down from their thrones, lay away their robes, put off their broidered garments, and clothe themselves with trembling, sitting on the ground astonished. They shall take up a lamentation, asking how she is destroyed, that renowned city inhabited of seafaring men which was strong in the sea and caused terror on all who haunted it. This parallels the fall of the great seafaring city that reflects Esau's nation today. -

The Most High will make Tyrus a desolate city like cities uninhabited, bring up the deep upon her, and cover her with great waters, bringing her down with them that descend into the pit to the low parts of the earth. He is putting the whole island and civilization under water forever. He will make her a terror, and she shall be no more; though she be sought for, she shall never be found again, because she said Aha when we suffered judgment. The city once beautiful and top-notch is wiped out because of how it mocked the judgment of the Most High. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake. The Lord roars from Zion and utters his voice from Jerusalem, so that the habitations of the shepherds mourn and the top of Carmel withers. This chapter was read straight through without going precept upon precept.

For three transgressions of Damascus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron. He will send a fire into the house of Hazael that shall devour the palaces of Benhadad, break the bar of Damascus, cut off the inhabitants of the plain of Aven and the sceptre from the house of Eden, and the people of Syria shall go into captivity unto Kir.

For three transgressions of Gaza and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they carried away the whole captivity to deliver them up to Edom. He will send a fire on the wall of Gaza that shall devour its palaces, cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod and the sceptre from Ashkelon, turn his hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish.

For three transgressions of Tyrus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom and did not remember the brotherly covenant. He will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus that shall devour its palaces.

For three transgressions of Edom and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because Edom pursued his brother with the sword, cast off all pity, and kept his wrath forever. He will send a fire upon Teman that shall devour the palaces of Bozrah.

For three transgressions of the children of Ammon and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they ripped up the women with child of Gilead to enlarge their border. He will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah that shall devour its palaces, with shouting in the day of battle and a tempest in the day of the whirlwind, and their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant)

The burden of Tyre calls the ships of Tarshish to howl, for the merchant harbor is laid waste with no house and no entering in. The merchants of Zidon who crossed the sea are silenced, the seed of Sihor and the harvest of the river was her revenue, and the report of Tyre brings sorrow as the report concerning Egypt did.

The inhabitants of the isle are told to pass over to Tarshish and howl, for this joyous city of ancient days is brought down, the crowning city whose merchants are princes and whose traffickers are the honourable of the earth. The Most High of hosts has purposed it, to stain the pride of all glory and bring into contempt all the honourable of the earth.

The Most High has stretched out His hand over the sea and shaken the kingdoms, giving a commandment against the merchant city to destroy its strongholds, so the oppressed virgin daughter of Zidon shall no more rejoice. The land of the Chaldeans is set forth as the example, brought to ruin, and again the ships of Tarshish are told to howl, for their strength is laid waste.

Tyre shall be forgotten seventy years, according to the days of one king, and afterward shall sing as a harlot to be remembered, committing fornication with all the kingdoms of the world. Yet at the end her merchandise and her hire shall be holiness to the Most High, not treasured nor laid up, but for them that dwell before Him to eat sufficiently and for durable clothing.

The burden of the word of the Lord in the land of Hadrach, and Damascus shall be the rest thereof: when the eyes of man, as of all the tribes of Israel, shall be toward the Lord. Tyrus did build herself a strong hold, and heaped up silver as the dust, and fine gold as the mire of the streets. Behold, the Lord will cast her out, and he will smite her power in the sea; and she shall be devoured with fire. Ashkelon shall see it, and fear; Gaza also shall see it, and be very sorrowful, and Ekron, for her expectation shall be ashamed; and the king shall perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon shall not be inhabited. These nations are judged for the part they had in the captivity, and they had a part. He that remaineth, even he, shall be for our God, and he shall be as a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite. Those that remain are the ones who will reverence Israel and serve.
I will encamp about mine house because of the army, because of him that passeth by, and because of him that returneth: and no oppressor shall pass through them any more.

Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass. That is how you know the verse is speaking of Christ, and salvation is what Israel is waiting on him to bring. He shall speak peace unto the heathen: and his dominion shall be from sea even to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the earth.

As for thee also, by the blood of thy covenant I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water. Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope: even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee. We are the prisoners of hope even now.

When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece, and made thee as the sword of a mighty man. The Lord shall be seen over them, and his arrow shall go forth as the lightning: and the Lord God shall blow the trumpet, and shall go with whirlwinds of the south. The Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people: for they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land.

verses.text: Son of man, say unto the prince of Tyrus, Thus saith the Lord God; Because thine heart is lifted up, and thou hast said, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas; yet thou art a man, and not God, though thou set thine heart as the heart of God:
Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee:
With thy wisdom and with thine understanding thou hast gotten thee riches, and hast gotten gold and silver into thy treasures:
By thy great wisdom and by thy traffick hast thou increased thy riches, and thine heart is lifted up because of thy riches:
Therefore thus saith the Lord God; Because thou hast set thine heart as the heart of God;
Behold, therefore I will bring strangers upon thee, the terrible of the nations: and they shall draw their swords against the beauty of thy wisdom, and they shall defile thy brightness.
They shall bring thee down to the pit, and thou shalt die the deaths of them that are slain in the midst of the seas.
Wilt thou yet say before him that slayeth thee, I am God? but thou shalt be a man, and no God, in the hand of him that slayeth thee.
Thou shalt die the deaths of the uncircumcised by the hand of strangers: for I have spoken it, saith the Lord God.

By the multitude of thy merchandise they have filled the midst of thee with violence, and thou hast sinned: therefore I will cast thee as profane out of the mountain of God: and I will destroy thee, O covering cherub, from the midst of the stones of fire.
Thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty, thou hast corrupted thy wisdom by reason of thy brightness: I will cast thee to the ground, I will lay thee before kings, that they may behold thee.

Thou hast defiled thy sanctuaries by the multitude of thine iniquities, by the iniquity of thy traffick; therefore will I bring forth a fire from the midst of thee, it shall devour thee, and I will bring thee to ashes upon the earth in the sight of all them that behold thee.
All they that know thee among the people shall be astonished at thee: thou shalt be a terror, and never shalt thou be any more.
Son of man, because that Tyrus hath said against Jerusalem, Aha, she is broken that was the gates of the people: she is turned unto me: I shall be replenished, now she is laid waste:
Therefore thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I am against thee, O Tyrus, and will cause many nations to come up against thee, as the sea causeth his waves to come up.
And they shall destroy the walls of Tyrus, and break down her towers: I will also scrape her dust from her, and make her like the top of a rock.

Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Tyrus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom, and remembered not the brotherly covenant:
But I will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus, which shall devour the palaces thereof.
Who hath taken this counsel against Tyre, the crowning city, whose merchants are princes, whose traffickers are the honourable of the earth?
The Lord of hosts hath purposed it, to stain the pride of all glory, and to bring into contempt all the honourable of the earth.
And Tyrus did build herself a strong hold, and heaped up silver as the dust, and fine gold as the mire of the streets.
Behold, the Lord will cast her out, and he will smite her power in the sea; and she shall be devoured with fire.

lawsResolved.text: Pride and arrogance brings decline, punishment and destruction.
A haughty heart leads to destruction.
There is but one God, the LORD God the Father.
Punishment will come to those who attempt to gain by deceit.
Do not glory or trust in your riches.
